Definition: from G1191; a Derbæan or inhabitant of Derbe:--of Derbe.
BiblicalUsage: Gaius of Derbe is the only man this word names, and he is listed among the companions who travelled with Paul toward Jerusalem. The word itself simply means a man of Derbe, a town in the hill country of Lycaonia.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the travelling companions are the quiet proof of the gospel's spread; ordinary believers from small towns like Derbe walked the roads with Paul, and their names in the record are worth remembering.
